🦖 Day 14 Development Log

🛠️ Technical Wins
 - I slowed the frame rate, 
 - Changed Theropoda to Tyrannosaurus rex
 - Changed fossil filtering so that the original fossil is fixed across time while the reconstructed fossils and tectonic plates
   unwind in deep time. 

💡 Insights: 
 - PBDB API can accommodate changes in taxonomic resolution as they have their own taxonomic tree. 
   Therefore I did not need to touch my order/family/genus columns.
 - Present-day fossils were previously being filtered out intentionally to show only species that were alive during their lifetime interval
   For the purposes of the museum demo however, I needed to keep the fossils on display even if they went extinct by that point.
   Both reconstructed and present-day fossils were filtered out based on this "extinct filter" applied here:
       # Step 1: Filter fossils
    filtered_df = fossil_df[
        (fossil_df['early_age'] >= reconstruction_time) #&
#        (fossil_df['late_age'] <= reconstruction_time)
    ]
   in fossils.py.
   By removing the late-age filter, I was effectively ignoring extinction and the fossils were allowed to persist from the time they first walked the Earth as dinosaurs.

🧭 Next steps: 
 - Check if fossils are mislabeled between present vs reconstructed fossils as present-day fossils are splitting weirdly around 35-40 Ma
 - Replace fossil blips with T. rex .png
 - Land coloured green and ocean coloured blue
 - (optional) Dynamic legend with respect to dinosaur chosen
